Figure 10 of the original SEB paper compares linear chains assembled from
Gaussian polymers, thin rods, Gaussian loops, and thin circles. It also shows
that the choice of reference point is part of the model: joining fixed ends is
not equivalent to joining independently sampled positions on two contours.

![Published Figure 10: form factors for linear chains assembled from different subunits and reference-point choices.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/main/PaperFigs/fig10.png){fig-alt="Published Figure 10 comparing endpoint-linked and contour-linked linear chains of Gaussian polymers, thin rods, Gaussian loops, and thin circles." width="90%"}

The paper uses 100 subunits per chain. The executable comparison below uses 12
so the documentation remains quick to rebuild. Set `segment_count = 100` to
reproduce the published chain length.

## Build a reusable chain function

Every instance receives a unique name but shares the tag `segment`. The tag
reduces the complete chain to one excess scattering length and one structural
size parameter.

For a distributed reference such as `contour`, the suffix after `#` identifies
one sampled attachment. Different suffixes on the two sides of every link make
the two contour positions statistically independent.

```{python}
import math

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pyseb


def build_chain(model, left_reference, right_reference, segment_count):
    world = pyseb.World(f"Figure10-{model}-{left_reference}")
    graph = world.Add(model, "segment1", "segment")

    for index in range(2, segment_count + 1):
        current = f"segment{index}.{left_reference}"
        previous = f"segment{index - 1}.{right_reference}"
        if left_reference == "contour":
            current += f"#left{index}"
        if right_reference == "contour":
            previous += f"#right{index - 1}"
        world.Link(model, current, previous, "segment")

    world.Add(graph, "chain")
    return world
```

## Match the single-subunit size

Each case below has single-subunit $R_g^2=1$, matching the comparison used for
the publication figure. Loops and circles have no fixed ends, so they only
appear in the contour-linked cases.

```{python}
segment_count = 12

cases = [
    ("Polymer: end to end", "GaussianPolymer", "end1", "end2",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "Rg_segment": 1.0}),
    ("Polymer: contour to contour", "GaussianPolymer", "contour", "contour",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "Rg_segment": 1.0}),
    ("Rod: end to end", "ThinRod", "end1", "end2",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "L_segment": math.sqrt(12.0)}),
    ("Rod: contour to contour", "ThinRod", "contour", "contour",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "L_segment": math.sqrt(12.0)}),
    ("Loop: contour to contour", "GaussianLoop", "contour", "contour",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "Rg_segment": 1.0}),
    ("Circle: contour to contour", "ThinCircle", "contour", "contour",
     {"beta_segment": 1.0, "R_segment": math.sqrt(2.0)}),
]

chains = {
    label: (build_chain(model, left, right, segment_count), parameters)
    for label, model, left, right, parameters in cases
}

print(f"built {len(chains)} chains with {segment_count} subunits each")
```

## Evaluate the form factors

```{python}
q = np.geomspace(1e-2, 50.0, 72)
curves = {
    label: np.asarray(world.EvaluateFormFactor("chain", parameters, q.tolist()))
    for label, (world, parameters) in chains.items()
}
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-figure10-linear-chain-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Form factors for six 12-subunit chains. Increase segment_count to 100 for the published chain length."

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for label, values in curves.items():
    axis = axes[0] if "end to end" in label else axes[1]
    axis.loglog(q, values, label=label.split(":")[0])

axes[0].set_title("Fixed endpoint links")
axes[1].set_title("Distributed contour links")
for axis in axes:
    axis.set_xlabel(r"$q$")
    axis.legend(fontsize="small")
axes[0].set_ylabel(r"$F(q)$")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The chains agree at sufficiently small q because every normalized form factor
approaches one. Their intermediate- and high-q behavior separates the local
subunit shape from the statistics introduced by the selected references.

## What this demonstrates

- A subunit type and a linking reference are independent modeling choices.
- Tags share physical parameters without merging instance identities.
- Distributed-reference suffixes control whether attachments are shared or
  independently averaged.
- The same chain-building loop works for any subunit exposing compatible
  references.
